title: Pullback of coherent formal modules
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of Noetherian schemes, $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and $\mathcal I=f^{-1}\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal O_X$. (1) For an object $(\mathcal G_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}(Y,\mathcal J)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] the system $(f^*\mathcal G_n)$ [def-pc-module-pullback], with the pulled back transition maps, is an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$; this defines a functor $f^*:\mathit{Coh}(Y,\mathcal J)\to\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$. (2) For a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal G$ [pqf-def-coherent] there is a natural isomorphism $f^*(\mathcal G^\wedge)\cong(f^*\mathcal G)^\wedge$; when $f$ is the inclusion of an open subscheme $U\subseteq Y$, $f^*$ is restriction to $U$, so $(\mathcal G^\wedge)|_U=(\mathcal G|_U)^\wedge$.

proof.text: Construct the all-power quotient isomorphism using the equality of image subobjects from [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-power-product-image]. The subobject equality gives an isomorphism of product inclusions; compose the resulting cokernel isomorphism with cokernel-of-image and preservation of cokernels by tensor pullback (its recorded adjunction). This yields sigma with projection equation. For any linear map and any pair m >= n, precompose both naturality composites with the quotient projection; the cokernel descent equation and the projection equation give equality. Cancel the epimorphism.

A coherent module is quasi-coherent of finite type. Transfer the standard pullback quasi-coherence instance along uniqueness of left adjoints to pushforward, and use the dedicated finite-type pullback theorem. Apply the locally Noetherian coherence criterion on X. This proves coherence of every pulled-back term.

If the original ideal-power product is zero, its inclusion is zero and its cokernel projection is an isomorphism. Its pullback is an isomorphism. The projection equation for sigma makes the target quotient projection an isomorphism too. Cancel this monomorphism in the cokernel condition: the target product inclusion is zero. Since that inclusion is monic, its source is zero. For each transition, compose sigma with the pullback of its original quotient-to-term isomorphism; the projection equation verifies the transition factorization. Together these prove the formal-system object conditions.

Lift the termwise whiskering functor to the full subcategory of coherent formal systems using those object conditions. Lift tensor pullback to coherent modules using the coherence proof. Both composites with their inclusions are definitionally the specified functors. The same all-power naturality equation gives a natural isomorphism of completed systems, natural both in level and in the coherent module. Cancel the fully faithful inclusion of coherent formal systems to lift that isomorphism.

For an open immersion, tensor pullback and restriction are left adjoints of the same pushforward; their uniqueness isomorphism identifies them. Whisker the completion comparison with this isomorphism and its inverse on the two sides to obtain the required ambient restriction comparison. No separate preservation-of-products statement for restriction or structure-sheaf comparison is needed.

split_report.summary: Statement kept (it is the first assertion of Stacks 0887 without right exactness and the flat case, which no user cites, plus the identity f^*(G^) = (f^*G)^ of the proof of 088B). Proof in seven steps following the computation of the 0887 proof: the extended ideal and its powers, the quotient computation f^*(G/J^nG) = f^*G/I^n f^*G (new node lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient, the right-exactness argument of the Stacks proof, unsplit), coherence of f^*G_n (01XZ, 01BG via the closed node, 01B6 via lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type), I^n f^*G_n = 0, the transition isomorphisms, functoriality, part (2) with compatibility with transition maps and naturality, and the open-immersion case (I = J|_U). The Stacks display has I and J interchanged (misprint).
